# ui::Binding

Header: `winui/core/Property.hpp`.

```cpp
template <typename T> class Binding
```

A spec field's value: either a constant or a live binding to a [Property](property.md), told apart in the source.

A plain value converts implicitly and is a constant, set once. A [Property](property.md) or a [Computed](computed.md) written into the field binds it: `.text = name` follows `name` from then on, two-way on an editable field. [bind()](namespace-ui.md#bind) is for the rest: a conversion (`ui::bind(clicks, fn)`), several sources, and [bind_one_way()](namespace-ui.md#bind_one_way). `name.get()` is the current value as a constant. A spec's [build()](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#build) consumes it, subscribing the built control when it is [reactive()](#reactive).

Copyable: one binding can go into several fields, and each control that builds from a copy subscribes on its own, so it follows the property for as long as it lives. A two-way binding copied into several editable fields writes back from each of them, and the equality gate keeps them from writing to each other in turn.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::string> title{"Untitled"};
ui::Property<int>         clicks{0};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::Text{.text = "static label"}, // a value: set once, never tracked
    ui::Text{.text = title},          // a binding: tracked
    ui::Text{.text = ui::bind(clicks, [](int n) { return std::format("Clicks: {}", n); })},
}});
title = "Report.txt"; // the second Text updates

ui::Binding<std::string> name = ui::bind(title); // one binding, two fields
ui::VerticalStack{.content = {ui::TextBox{.text = name}, ui::Text{.text = name}}};
```

## element_type

```cpp
using ui::Binding< T >::element_type = typename detail::BindingSource<T>::Element
```

For a binding of a `std::vector`, its element type; an empty placeholder type otherwise.

## Attach

```cpp
using ui::Binding< T >::Attach = std::function<Subscription(Callback<void(T)>, T* now)>
```

The reactive form's subscribe thunk: hands a sink to the source property and returns the resulting [Subscription](subscription.md) for the built [Element](../tree/element.md) to own. When `now` is not null it first stores the source's value of this moment there; an empty sink only reads.

## Write

```cpp
using ui::Binding< T >::Write = std::function<void(const T&)>
```

The two-way form's write thunk: stores a value the user entered back into the source.

## Binding

```cpp
Binding() = default
```

A constant value-initialized T.

## Binding

```cpp
Binding(T value)
```

A plain value. Implicit, so `.text = title` works as written.

## Binding

```cpp
template <typename U>
Binding(U&& value)
    requires (!std::same_as<std::remove_cvref_t<U>, T> && !std::same_as<std::remove_cvref_t<U>, Binding> && std::convertible_to<U, T>)
```

A plain value of another type that converts to T, so a field that is a `Binding<std::optional<Color>>` takes [`colors::White`](namespace-ui-colors.md#white) (two user-defined conversions in a row otherwise, which C++ refuses), a `Binding<float>` takes an int and a `Binding<std::size_t>` a non-negative int, and a `Binding<std::string>` a string literal. A conversion that would lose the value does not compile: a pointer or a number into a bool field, a floating-point number into an integer one, an integer into a narrower one.

## Binding

```cpp
template <typename A, typename B, typename... Rest>
Binding(A&& a, B&& b, Rest&& ... rest)
    requires (!std::same_as<std::remove_cvref_t<B>, Attach>) && (std::constructible_from<T, A, B, Rest...> || (detail::OptionalValue<T>::optional && std::constructible_from<typename detail::OptionalValue<T>::type, A, B, Rest...>))
```

A value built in place from a braced list of its constructor's arguments, so a field takes `{a, b}` as a plain field of its value type would, and an optional field as its value type would.

## Binding

```cpp
Binding(std::initializer_list<element_type> elements)
    requires requires(const detail::BindingSource<T>& source) { source.collection; }
```

For a binding of a vector: its elements as a braced list, so `.items = {"Inbox", "Sent"}` needs no `std::vector<std::string>` spelled out.

## Binding

```cpp
Binding(T initial, Attach attach)
```

The reactive form. [bind()](namespace-ui.md#bind) builds it; callers never spell it out.

## Binding

```cpp
Binding(T initial, Attach attach, Write write)
```

A two-way binding: reactive, and able to write a new value back into its source. What [bind()](namespace-ui.md#bind) makes from a non-const [Property](property.md).

## Binding

```cpp
Binding(T initial, Attach attach, Write write, const void* group)
    requires requires(const detail::BindingSource<T>& source) { source.group; }
```

A two-way binding of a bool that also names the group of choices it is one of; what [ui::selects()](namespace-ui.md#selects) makes.

## Binding

```cpp
Binding(ObservableVector<element_type>* collection, typename detail::BindingSource<T>::Snapshot snapshot, Attach attach)
    requires requires(const detail::BindingSource<T>& source) { source.collection; }
```

A binding of a vector that also names the collection it came from; what [bind()](namespace-ui.md#bind) of a [ui::ObservableVector](observable-vector.md) makes. `snapshot` copies the collection into [initial()](#initial) the first time it is asked; null leaves it empty (an item type that cannot be copied).

## Binding

```cpp
template <typename S>
Binding(S& source)
    requires (detail::is_source<S> && detail::PropertyBindsTo<detail::source_value_t<S>, T>) || detail::is_collection_of<S, T>
```

A [Property](property.md), a [Computed](computed.md) or an [ObservableVector](observable-vector.md), bound: `.text = name` is the same as `.text = ui::bind(name)`, `.items = todos` as `.items = ui::bind(todos)`. A writable [Property](property.md) is two-way on an editable field, as [bind()](namespace-ui.md#bind) is; a `const` [Property](property.md) and a [Computed](computed.md) are one-way. A source of another type converts as a [bind()](namespace-ui.md#bind) of it would.

## Binding

```cpp
template <typename U>
Binding(Binding<U> other)
    requires (!std::same_as<U, T>) && std::convertible_to<const U&, T> && (detail::binding_value_converts<U, T>())
```

A binding of another type that converts to T, still reactive: a `Binding<std::string>` takes a [bind()](namespace-ui.md#bind) whose function returns a string literal, a `Binding<double>` a [`Property<int>`](property.md), a `Binding<std::optional<bool>>` a [`Property<bool>`](property.md). The conversions a plain value refuses (a number into a bool, a floating-point number into an integer, an integer into a narrower one) are refused here too.

A two-way binding stays two-way when the value converts back without loss, as between float and double: a [Slider](../controls/slider.md#uislider)'s `value` takes [`ui::bind()`](namespace-ui.md#bind) of a [`Property<float>`](property.md), and what the user drags is written back as a float. Otherwise the result is one-way, and an editable field ([TwoWayField](two-way-field.md)) refuses it at compile time.

## Binding

```cpp
Binding(const Binding&) = default
```

A copy subscribes on its own when its field is built; see the class comment.

## operator=

```cpp
Binding& operator=(const Binding&) = default
```

Same as the copy constructor.

## Binding

```cpp
Binding(Binding&& other)
```

Takes `other`'s value and thunks; `other` is left a constant.

## operator=

```cpp
Binding& operator=(Binding&& other)
```

Same as the move constructor.

## initial

```cpp
const T& initial() const
```

The value as of construction: what a control is initialized with, whether or not this binding is reactive. For a binding of an [ObservableVector](observable-vector.md), a copy of the collection made the first time it is asked, so a field that reads the collection in place ([observable()](#observable)) never makes one.

## current

```cpp
T current() const
```

The value the source holds right now: what a control that subscribes later than the binding was made starts from, since a property may have changed in between. [initial()](#initial) for a constant.

## reactive

```cpp
bool reactive() const noexcept
```

True if this came from [bind()](namespace-ui.md#bind) and will keep delivering values; false for a constant.

## subscribe

```cpp
Subscription subscribe(Callback<void(T)> sink)
```

Start tracking. Only valid when [reactive()](#reactive); the returned [Subscription](subscription.md) must outlive the interest in `sink`. Callers use [ui::apply()](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#apply) (ui/spec/Common.hpp) instead, which also sets the initial value.

## writable

```cpp
bool writable() const noexcept
```

True when the binding can write back into its source: [bind()](namespace-ui.md#bind) of a non-const [Property](property.md) with no conversion, or one turned into a field type it converts back from without loss.

## take_writer

```cpp
Write take_writer() noexcept
```

The write thunk, moved out for the control that will call it; empty for a one-way binding. An editable field's [build()](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#build) takes it ([ui::write_back()](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#write_back)); a display field never does, which is what makes the same [bind()](namespace-ui.md#bind) one-way there.

## observable

```cpp
auto* observable() const noexcept
    requires requires(const detail::BindingSource<T>& source) { source.collection; }
```

For a binding of a vector: the [ui::ObservableVector](observable-vector.md) it was made from, or nullptr when it came from a plain vector or a [Property](property.md). A field that can follow single edits reads the collection through this instead of taking whole copies from [subscribe()](#subscribe).

## selection_group

```cpp
const void* selection_group() const noexcept
    requires requires(const detail::BindingSource<T>& source) { source.group; }
```

For a binding of a bool made by [ui::selects()](namespace-ui.md#selects): the property whose choices it is one of, the same for every binding of that property. Controls bound with the same group form one set of choices ([RadioButton](../controls/radio-button.md#uiradiobutton)). nullptr for any other binding.
